categories.name: Agent Frameworks
categories.description: Libraries to build a single agent: prompts, tool-calling, the reasoning loop.
categories.when: Use to build a single agent in code: prompting, tool-calling, the reasoning loop. Pick one as your foundation.

categories.name: Orchestration & Multi-Agent
categories.pick: Add when one agent isn't enough
categories.description: Coordinate roles, hand-offs, graphs and workflows across multiple agents.
categories.when: Use when one agent isn’t enough and you need several agents, roles, hand-offs, or a workflow/graph.

categories.name: Autonomous Agents
categories.description: Goal-driven agents that plan and execute long-running tasks on their own.
categories.when: Use when you want a goal-driven agent that plans and runs long tasks on its own (great as reference designs).

categories.name: Coding Agents
categories.description: Agents that read, write, refactor and ship software.
categories.when: Use when you want an agent that reads, writes, refactors and ships code in your repo or editor.

categories.name: Skills & Recipes
categories.pick: Add ready-made skills your agent can follow
categories.description: Reusable agent skills, opinionated harnesses and skill packs (Anthropic Skills, gstack, superpowers).
categories.when: Use to give your agent ready-made, reusable skills/recipes instead of hand-writing every behavior.

categories.name: Browser & Computer Use
categories.pick: Add to act in a browser / GUI
categories.description: Drive browsers, desktops and operating systems via clicks and vision.
categories.when: Use when your agent must act in a real browser, GUI, or desktop by seeing the screen and clicking.

categories.name: Memory & Knowledge
categories.pick: Add so your agent remembers & retrieves
categories.description: Long-term memory, retrieval (RAG) and vector stores for grounding.
categories.when: Use to give your agent long-term memory and retrieval over your own knowledge (RAG, vector stores).

categories.name: Data & Documents
categories.pick: Add to feed clean data to your agent
categories.description: Parse, extract, chunk and clean documents & web data for RAG and agents (markitdown, docling, unstructured).
categories.when: Use to turn messy docs, PDFs and web pages into clean, structured text your agent or RAG can consume.

categories.name: Tools & Protocols
categories.description: Standards and servers that connect agents to tools and to each other (MCP, A2A).
categories.when: Use to connect your agent to external tools and to other agents via standards like MCP and A2A.

categories.name: Sandboxes & MicroVMs
categories.pick: Add to run agent code safely
categories.description: Isolated microVM & sandbox runtimes where agents execute code and tools safely (E2B, Firecracker, microsandbox).
categories.when: Use when your agent runs untrusted code or tools and you need an isolated, safe place to execute it.

categories.name: Observability & Eval
categories.description: Trace, evaluate, monitor and debug agent behavior in dev and prod.
categories.when: Use to trace, evaluate and monitor what your agent actually did — in development and in production.

categories.name: Runtimes & Platforms
categories.pick: Use to assemble without much code
categories.description: Low-code builders, workflow automation and hosting for agents.
categories.when: Use to assemble or host an agent with little-to-no code: low-code builders, workflow automation, hosting.

categories.name: Voice & Speech
categories.pick: Add for speech in / speech out
categories.description: Speech recognition (Whisper/ASR), text-to-speech, and realtime conversational audio.
categories.when: Use when your agent needs to listen (speech-to-text), talk (text-to-speech), or hold a live voice call.

categories.name: Models & Serving
categories.pick: Pick a model + a way to run it
categories.description: Run, host, quantize and route the LLMs your agent thinks with. Infra, not agents.
categories.when: Use when you want to run or host the LLM yourself — your own hardware or cloud — instead of calling a hosted API.

categories.name: Open Models
categories.pick: Pick the open-weight model your agent runs on
categories.description: Open-weight LLMs from Hugging Face, ranked by community likes and downloads.
categories.when: Use to choose the actual open-weight model — DeepSeek, Llama, Qwen, gpt-oss — that your agent reasons with, then run it with a tool from Models & Serving.
